+# Potency lens: #1063, DEV-net-f, head b660205
+
+Record: PR #1063 · package DEV-net-f · head b660205
+
+Scope: the whole PR at b660205 (L3 accept in [comment 6117696547](https://github.com/ghbmrk/agentOS/pull/1063#issuecomment-6117696547)). Tier A.
+
+Question: where does the change cap capability without buying matching security or UX?
+
+- Pass: the access point's interface joins the exempt set at bring-up, so the owner's phone reaches the local page over the box's Wi-Fi (A1) instead of joining a network whose page never loads.
+- Pass: the add is idempotent and runs on each bring-up, so a recreated interface is let through again at no cost.
+- Pass: the wireless-only check costs nothing on a box whose access point is its only Wi-Fi radio.
+
+Findings: blocker 0; release 0 (R1 is Security's); later 0.
+
+Arbitration: no tension with Security or UX. R1(b) and R1(c) narrow the exemption to the AP's lifetime and identity and remove nothing the owner uses.

+Verdict: sign-off
+
+# Security lens: #1063, DEV-net-f, head b660205
+
+Record: PR #1063 · package DEV-net-f · head b660205
+
+Scope: the whole PR at b660205 (L3 accept with threat check in [comment 6117696547](https://github.com/ghbmrk/agentOS/pull/1063#issuecomment-6117696547)). Tier A. `go test -race ./localui/ ./netguard/` and `tests.test_image` pass locally; `tests/test_inbound_netns.py` ran under sudo in CI (5 ran, none skipped); locally it skips (no `ip` binary). Six mutants (add failure ignored in the script and in `BringUp`, wildcard exempt, wireless check dropped, `create element`, `BindsTo=` removed) are all killed.
+
+Question: can an adversary get an interface other than the access point through `agentos_inbound`, and does every failure leave the drop in place?
+
+- Pass, naming: one argument, the kernel charset, 15 characters or fewer, no leading `-`; `ExemptUnit` uses the same `ifaceRe` and systemd escaping, so a name cannot inject into nft or the unit. Renaming needs CAP_NET_ADMIN on the host. A rename away from the AP name is dropped (netns test).
+- Pass, ordering: `Requires=`/`After=agentos-inbound.service`; a restart propagates through `Requires=`, and `nft -f` without a flush keeps the elements.
+- Pass, fail closed: a missing table, a failed add or a failed read-back exits 1 with the ruleset unchanged; `BringUp` never starts the AP after a failed unit.
+- Release, scope and lifetime: `iifname @exempt accept` admits every port on the interface, and only CH-9's `agentos_ap` (not yet loaded by anything) limits it to the page, DNS and DHCP. The exemption is added before `ap.Start`, is never removed (no `ExecStop`), and is granted to any `phy80211` interface the loader names. Nothing calls `BringUp` or starts the unit yet, so this is not reachable today.
+
+Findings: blocker 0; release 1 (R1: before P2-1 wires `BringUp`, (a) load `agentos_ap` first or remove the element when `ap.Start` fails, (b) remove the element when the AP stops, (c) admit only the interface the loader created as the AP. Invariant A14 / DEV-2 In. Failure path: a single-radio box stops its AP and `wlan0` joins the home Wi-Fi as a station while still exempt, so home hosts reach every box port. R1c is the builder's second-card gap, classed release under OPERATING §2); later 0.
+
+Arbitration: no tension with Potency or UX.

+Verdict: sign-off

+# UX lens: #1063, DEV-net-f, head b660205
+
+Record: PR #1063 · package DEV-net-f · head b660205
+
+Scope: the whole PR at b660205 (L3 accept in [comment 6117696547](https://github.com/ghbmrk/agentOS/pull/1063#issuecomment-6117696547)). Owner-visible effects only: the access point's page becoming reachable, and what a failed bring-up says.
+
+Question: does it ask the owner for attention, time, decisions, memory, checking or recovery that the system could carry?
+
+- Pass: the owner does nothing; the exemption is added at each bring-up, including after the interface is recreated.
+- Pass: a failure says `agentos-ap-exempt: FAIL <reason>; the access point stays closed` on the journal and console, and `BringUp` returns it, so the box can say why its Wi-Fi did not come up.
+
+Findings:
+- **Later** `DEV-net-f l1`: `BringUp`'s error names the systemd unit; the P2-1 loader must map it to fixed owner text (CH-12).
+
+Findings: blocker 0; release 0; later 1.
+
+Arbitration: no tension with Security or Potency.
